newsitem.title: USA: Glaxo says FDA releases Epivir.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo says FDA releases Epivir.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc said Monday that the Food and Drug Administration has released Epivir (Lamivudine) under traditional regulations for use in combination with Retrovir.

The FDA decision was made on the strength of an international study which recently showed Epivir to be effective in reducing the risk of death and disease progression in persons with AIDS, the company said.
Epivir was originally released by the FDA in November 1995, under the agency's accelerated approval regulations, for use with Retrovir (zidovudine) in treating HIV and AIDS.

"This action is important in that it recognizes that Epivir has a significant impact on survival and delaying the progression of HIV infection," said Richard Kent, vice president and director of worldwide clinical development for Glaxo Wellcome in a statement.

The move to traditional regulatory clearance for Epivir was based on results of the CAESAR trial which was initiated in March, 1995 and discontinued in July, 1996, following an interim review of the data by an independent Data Safety and Monitoring Board, the company said.

Glaxo said the study showed that a significantly lower proportion of patients- 9.6 percent versus 19.6 percent- had at least one HIV disease progression event or death when they were assigned to add Epivir to current therapy compared with adding placebo to current therapy.
Prior to adding Epivir, all patients in the study were receiving Retrovir, either alone or in combination with didanosine or zalcitabine, the company said.

It said that in order to gain traditional regulatory clearance, it was necessary to demonstrate the drug's ability to positively impact so-called clinical endpoints -- survival and disease progression.
